newsitem.title: UK: UK DTI begins legal action to ban Barings chiefs.
newsitem.headline: UK DTI begins legal action to ban Barings chiefs.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry said on Sunday it had begun legal proceedings which could ban the former deputy chairman of collapsed merchant bank Barings and nine of its other directors from involvement in companies for 15 years.
A DTI spokeswoman said legal notifications had been sent to the former Baring chiefs late on Friday.

Former deputy chairman Andrew Tuckey and the nine other ex-directors, including former chief executive Peter Norris, have been told that action was being taken under the UK Company Directors Disqualification Act.
The spokeswoman said a preliminary hearing would be held in which the "evidence will be considered" and a timetable for a final hearing could be set afterwards.
No date or location had been set for the first hearing.
Peter Baring, the bank's former chairman, would not be included under the action, said the spokeswoman.
Barings collapsed in 1995 after Singapore-based trader Nick Leeson ran up unauthorised trading losses of more than 800 million stg.
Leeson is currently serving a jail sentence in Singapore after admitting charges of fraud.
